source_fields.instance: The environment precommits to ℓ_t ∈ B₂ᵈ(1). The learner chooses x_t ∈ B₂ᵈ(1), incurs ⟨x_t,ℓ_t⟩, and observes that value exactly. No independent observation noise is added.

source_fields.adversary_information: The environment fixes the complete loss sequence before interaction. It may know the algorithm and public parameters but cannot depend on the learner's private seed. This is an oblivious environment; nonanticipation describes the learner's causal information and does not extend the specification to a history-adaptive adversary.
unresolved_applicability: The 2026 lower bound includes minimum operators, truncations, and dimension–horizon conditions. The unconditional √(dT) shorthand in an abstract cannot replace these across the full parameter domain.

operations.query_signature: Input: $t,\ x_t\in B_2^d(1)$. The specification's protocol governs timing and visible information.
operations.order_convention: order is relative to the current member f_t(x), f(x), or sample F(x;ξ_t) of the named indexed function family and only with respect to x; finite feedback interfaces have no derivative order

feedback_quality.description: The current loss $\ell_t$ is fixed before $x_t$ is chosen. Each round returns one exact scalar, with no independent observation noise. A second direction cannot be queried against the same loss.

operations.coupling: The current loss $\ell_t$ is fixed before $x_t$ is chosen. Each round returns one exact scalar, with no independent observation noise. A second direction cannot be queried against the same loss.
operations.index_control: The learner selects feasible actions and any probes permitted by the specification. The environment determines current losses, outcomes, or fresh samples. The learner cannot select future rounds.
operations.access_schedule: Interaction follows the sequence in registry.protocols. Current loss feedback is available only after the action is submitted. Any pre-action disclosure of context or advice is specified separately.

public_inputs: Per-round loss-vector norm bound of one
auxiliary_interfaces: No additional access to hidden losses, means, or gradients is available. Projection, sampling, and internal optimization over public domains may have separately recorded computation costs; they are not free loss oracles.

source_fields.feasibility: Every loss-bearing action must belong to the action domain. The final output retains the complete action trajectory.
source_fields.allowed_postprocessing: Any measurable computation on received feedback is allowed. No native observation may be added after the budget is exhausted or the algorithm stops.
source_fields.certificate_requirement: Only the stated statistical guarantee is required, not a certificate verifiable through the feedback interface.

source_fields.normalization: Use the cumulative quantity over T rounds without dividing by T. Preserve the displayed order of probability or expectation.
source_fields.finiteness_conditions: The unit mean/loss range or the stated Lipschitz amplitude bound limits the per-round excess loss to two. Cumulative regret is therefore at most 2T. Unbounded observation noise does not enter pseudo-regret.

components.description: Sequential online rounds; only information permitted by the protocol is visible in each round.
One exact scalar per round, for $T$ bandit observations in total.

source_fields.budget_semantics: There are T sequential interaction rounds. Native feedback count is determined by the per-round protocol and is not an independent budget to minimize.
source_fields.scalarization: Retain the native objective and complete resource vector. At fixed $T$, compare cumulative regret. Best-arm-identification stopping times and error probabilities use their own task-specific criteria.
source_fields.setup_cost: Only declared public inputs may be read. Hidden losses, means, or samples cannot be accessed in advance or outside the $T$ rounds or $\tau$ samples.
source_fields.online_cost: Any causal randomized algorithm is allowed. The available OSMD upper bound uses internal random exploration and regularized updates. Internal linear algebra and domain optimization are separate from the native scalar-feedback count; computational efficiency is not claimed for the entire admissible class.
source_fields.amortization_scope: The algorithm runs on one environment. Charged feedback cannot be reused across independent instances.
source_fields.precision_model: Observations and internal arithmetic use the exact-real model. No bit-complexity claim follows.

view_override_policy.limitations: Mechanical merge does not certify consistency or mathematical identity. Narrative qualifications and source conditions remain authoritative.

source_fields.randomization: Private randomization is allowed. The seed is hidden from the environment and independent of the fixed instance and sample randomness.
source_fields.adaptivity: The action and every probe in a round may depend only on previous-round feedback, public inputs, any context or advice already revealed that round, and private randomness. They may not use unrevealed current losses or samples.
restrictions: All measurable causal policies satisfying the declared information timing and feasible domain are allowed, without extra span, iteration-form, or polynomial-time restrictions.
source_fields.internal_computation: Arbitrary causal randomized algorithms and measurable exact-real internal work are allowed. OSMD uses internal random exploration and regularized updates. Linear algebra and domain optimization are separate from scalar feedback. Neither computational efficiency of the entire class nor arithmetic/bit bounds are implied.
source_fields.parallelism: Interaction proceeds in sequential time rounds. A two-point evaluation is one pair of same-round responses only where explicitly permitted; it is not equivalent to two independent rounds.

source_fields.complete_expression: The native target is $\inf_{\mathcal A}\sup_{\ell_{1:T}\in(B_2^d(1))^T}\mathbb E_{\mathcal A}[R_T]$.
aggregation_order: First take the infimum over complete nonanticipating learning policies using only public inputs.
Then take the supremum over instances fixed before interaction that satisfy the stated model.
Expectation includes learner randomness and, when present, observation noise or random samples.
The objective fixes the comparator. Per-round optimal actions, a fixed action, and a sample-path optimum are not interchangeable.
source_fields.quantifier_order: One learning algorithm must apply to every instance in the declared class. It may use public inputs only, not hidden instance parameters.
source_fields.time_uniformity: The horizon T is fixed and public. The guarantee holds for that T; it does not automatically give an anytime result or a simultaneous high-probability statement for all T.

description_paragraphs: The learner chooses an action in the unit ball and incurs and observes its exact inner product with the current bounded loss vector. The vectors are fixed in advance, and each round supplies one scalar; there is no additional independent additive noise.

description_paragraphs: The hidden linear loss vectors obey $\|\ell_t\|_2\le1$ in every round.
The sole loss-incurring point is $x_t$. Feedback is one projection value, not the complete loss vector.
The comparator is the best fixed point $u$ in the ball after observing the sequence, with minimum cumulative loss $-\|\sum_t\ell_t\|_2$.
Require $d,T\ge1$; the action domain is the Euclidean unit ball.
The adversary cannot replace per-round norm constraints with unbounded Gaussian losses.
